title_original: Roberto Rossellini Retrospectives Head to New York and L.A. for the Italian Neorealist Master’s 120th Birthday
excerpt_original: Film Forum in New York, the Italian Ministry of Culture, and Cinecittà will present Rossellini 120, a 25-film retrospective dedicated to Roberto Rossellini, opening November 20 at Film Forum.

blocks.text: Italian neorealist master Roberto Rossellini , though he died in 1977, turns 120 this year. In celebration, major retrospective series are coming up.

Film Forum in New York, the Italian Ministry of Culture, and Cinecittà will present “Rossellini 120,” a 25- film retrospective dedicated to Roberto Rossellini, opening at Film Forum on November 20. The retrospective will also open in Los Angeles on November 4 at the Academy Museum as “Roberto Rossellini Prefers Real Life,” courtesy of the Italian Ministry of Culture and Cinecittà.

Through December 10, New York’s Film Forum will host the 25-film “Rossellini 120.” The filmmaker’s daughter, Oscar-nominated actress Isabella Rossellini, will appear in person on November 20 with “Voyage to Italy” (which starred her mother, Ingrid Bergman, opposite George Sanders) and again on November 26 (i.e., Thanksgiving) with “Flowers of St. Francis” and “Europa ’51.” IndieWire shares exclusive details as well as a trailer for the retrospective above. The program is a partnership of Film Forum, Cinecittà, and the Italian Ministry of Culture

blocks.text: Rossellini is best known for his films with his third wife, Ingrid Bergman, including “Stromboli,” “Europe ’51,” “Fear,” “Journey to Italy,” and “Joan of Arc at the Stake.”

Isabella said, “Our family is coming en masse to see the retrospective at Film Forum. It’s an occasion for my sister Ingrid and I to show the films to the youngest family members, who never met their Nonno (grandfather) or bisnonno (great-grandfather), in the 120th year since his birth. We’re super-grateful to both Film Forum and Cinecittà, who for years have restored and presented our father’s work. His films continue to inspire filmmakers all around the world.”

The program includes Rossellini films “Rome, Open City,” “Paisan,” “Germany, Year Zero.” The lineup also includes Guy Maddin’s “My Dad Is 100 Years Old,” featuring Isabella Rossellini, and the documentaries “Viva Ingrid!” by Alessandro Rossellini and “Rossellini Through His Own Eyes” by Adriano Aprà.

Manuela Cacciamani, CEO of Cinecittà, added, “Film Forum has long been one of New York’s most beloved homes for repertory cinema, a place where generations of audiences have discovered the great masters of world film. It is the ideal setting for the work of Roberto Rossellini, who changed the language of cinema and whose films continue to speak powerfully to our present. Cinecittà has held the rights to ten of his most representative films for thirty years, restored in our own laboratories and preserved in valuable 35mm prints, which we are delighted to make exceptionally available for this occasion, that follows the steps of many joint past initiatives, like the legendary 1993 ‘Tutto Fellini.’ We thank our U.S. partners Janus Films and The Criterion Collection for their care in distributing Rossellini’s legacy through the years”.

Film Forum audiences will also see Cinecittà’s new 4K restoration of “Fear” from 1954, which was Rossellini’s last film with Bergman. The Film Forum series arrives a couple of weeks after the launch of “Rossellini Prefers Real Life” at the Academy Museum in Los Angeles, beginning November 4. Isabella and family will also be in attendance for that series, which includes the above films for West Coasters.
